Agent Name: Planner
Step Number: 10
Reason for Mistake: The Planner incorrectly concluded that the war with "over 60 million casualties" was World War I. In Step 10, after reviewing the Britannica page for World War I (which showed ~8.5 million military deaths and ~13 million civilian deaths, totaling ~21.5 million) and the World War II page (which showed 40-50 million lives claimed, with estimates ranging up to 60-85 million depending on the source), the Planner falsely asserted that "over 60 million" is a figure commonly associated with World War I. This is factually incorrect; the "over 60 million" figure is widely associated with World War II. Furthermore, the Planner ignored the clear evidence from the Livesey Hall War Memorial (Wikipedia and DuckDuckGo results) which explicitly states it commemorates both World War I and World War II. The Planner's error led to the wrong identification of the war in the final decision logic.
